newsitem.title: CHINA: Taiwan invests $360 mln in southwest China city.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan invests $360 mln in southwest China city.

text.p: Chengdu, capital of the southwest China province of Sichuan, has set up an investment zone for Taiwan companies which has attracted $360 million in promised investment from 27 Taiwan firms, the Liberation Daily said on Friday.

The zone, covering six sq km, is the first in China to be jointly invested, managed and promoted by both the Taiwan and Chinese sides and aims to attract a total of $1.2 billion in investment, the paper said.

Kao Ching-yuan, president of President Enterprises, visited the zone and immediately decided to set up a food processing firm there, the biggest of his firms in terms of scale in China, it said but gave no more details.
President is one of the largest Taiwan investors in China. Kao met China's President Jiang Zemin in Beijing late last month and Jiang assured him that Taiwan investments in China would be protected.
